beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secret store at runtime; never check the connection string into source control or write it to logs.

Reuse a single Motor/PyMongo client across the app (create once at startup and inject), set a sensible maxPoolSize/minPoolSize rather than creating a new client per request to avoid connection storms.
Enable TLS/SSL on the client connection and verify certificates (tls=true or tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) so traffic to the managed cluster is encrypted in transit.
Use least-privilege database credentials: create a dedicated DB user for the sample app with only the minimal roles (readWrite on sample_fintech_10) rather than using an admin/root account.

Store LLM outputs, derived classifications, and policy decisions with provenance fields (classifier_version, deterministic_fallback_flag, model_response, timestamp, source_report_id) so decisions are auditable and reproducible.

For expense reports with many small line items, embed the line_item array inside the parent report document (rather than separate collection) when typical array sizes are small (dozens) and you always fetch the whole report; avoid embedding huge arrays to stay well under the DB document size limit.

If you need to query or update individual line items frequently or arrays can grow large, model line items as a separate collection with report_id reference and index on report_id to keep single-document sizes small and make updates idempotent.

Create compound indexes that match the app’s common queries exactly (e.g., {company_id:1, report_status:1, submitted_at:-1}) so the query planner can use index prefixes; verify with explain() that indexes are used.
Add an index on any field used in sort operations (e.g., submitted_at) to avoid in-memory sorts and high memory utilization during queries.
Use partial or sparse indexes for optional or rare fields you query (e.g., policy_violation:true) to keep index size down and speed writes.
When adding or changing indexes in a production cluster, create them during off-peak windows and monitor impact; prefer online/background index builds when supported to avoid blocking writes.

For vector search, persist vectors as a numeric array field and create the appropriate vector index (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with matching parameters (distance metric: cosine or inner_product, M/ef_construction or ef_search) tuned to vector dimensionality and recall/latency needs.

Normalize the vector dimensionality (consistent embedding length) and store metadata fields indexed for filtering (e.g., company_id, report_id) so vector queries can be filtered by metadata before nearest-neighbour search.

Implement idempotency and optimistic concurrency for processing reports: use a processing_status field with atomic updates (findOneAndUpdate with a status filter) or include an etag/_id-based check to avoid double-processing when retries occur.

Use retry with exponential backoff for transient network and rate-limit errors; capture specific retryable exception classes from Motor/PyMongo and limit total retry time to avoid long blocking operations.

Avoid long-running transactions across many documents for the classifier pipeline; prefer single-document atomic updates or small multi-document transactions limited to what the MongoDB/Cosmos API supports.

Log queries that exceed a latency threshold and use explain() and the provider's tools (the provided MCP server tools) to inspect query plans and index usage; include timestamps and correlation ids in logs for each processed report.

Do not persist LLM API keys or plaintext credentials in the DB; if storing model-related config, store only non-sensitive version identifiers and minimal configuration and keep secrets in environment or Key Vault.

Seed test/demo data and create indexes programmatically (seed script + indexes module) against the specific database name (sample_fintech_10) but ensure scripts are idempotent (create_if_not_exists semantics) so repeated runs are safe.

Persist agent memory or consistent classification decisions in the DB with versioning and TTL for ephemeral session memory; include a deterministic fallback flag so replayable tests can run without an LLM key.
